name: Bupropion
summary: An activating, weight-neutral atypical antidepressant (NDRI) also used for smoking cessation; dose-dependent seizure risk limits the dose.
mechanism: Weakly inhibits dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake; minimal serotonin activity.

dosing.adult: XL: 150 mg once daily to start, increased to 300 mg once daily

safety.pregnancy: Limited data; an early signal for cardiovascular malformations was not confirmed.
contraindications: History of bulimia or anorexia nervosa
warnings: Black-box warning: increased suicidality in children, adolescents, and young adults (≤24 y) early in treatment
Dose-dependent seizure risk — keep to 450 mg/day maximum
Can raise blood pressure — caution when combined with nicotine patches
Activation and insomnia — can worsen anxiety
monitoring: Seizure-risk factors and adherence to the dose cap
Mood and suicidality early in treatment
safety.overdose: Seizures are the main risk (dose-dependent), plus tachycardia and agitation — overdose can be serious.

indications: Off-label: adjunct in bipolar depression, ADHD
clinicalPearls: Activating and free of sexual dysfunction — a good switch when SSRI fatigue or sexual side effects dominate.
Dose-dependent seizure risk — respect the 450 mg/day cap; avoid in epilepsy and eating disorders.
good: Depression with fatigue, or when SSRI sexual dysfunction or weight gain is an issue; smoking cessation.
bad: Seizure history, eating disorders, alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal, or anxiety-predominant presentations.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard psychopharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
